object_description: large isolated puristic cuboid with basement atriums and a central atrium
design_condition: The cuboid mediates between three distinct urban structures, maintaining distance from its surroundings while concentrating much of the program below ground and shaping several surrounding open spaces.

positive.statement: The stand-alone cuboid is well-proportioned, efficiently organized, and maintains sufficient distance from its surroundings.

position.rationale: Cuboid massing and isolation are clearly visible across the calibrated top and elevation views.

positive.statement: The forecourt-foyer-atrium sequence is smooth and impressive.

position.rationale: South-central approach and central void provide a constrained anchor for the sequential spatial experience.

positive.statement: The large atrium links teaching, research, and departments visually, functionally, and symbolically.

position.rationale: The central rectangular void is clearly legible in plan and aligned with the elevations.

positive.statement: The atrium provides an airy and spectacular central heart for the building.

position.rationale: Central atrium placement is corroborated by the top view and corresponding elevation openings.

positive.statement: The open-space concept creates usable areas with low sealing, effective rainwater management, and high biodiversity.

position.rationale: Perimeter open-space bands are visible around the isolated building footprint in the top view.

positive.statement: The building is clear and effectively organized inside.

position.rationale: Interior organization is not exposed, so the marker uses a distributed low-level building-surface approximation.

positive.statement: The construction costs are within the specifications.

position.rationale: Cost compliance has no useful geometric referent in the sampled model.

negative.statement: Enlarging the cuboid reduces and underdevelops the open space.

position.target: enlarged cuboid and reduced open space
position.rationale: The full cuboid envelope and its surrounding open-space margin are directly visible across all views.

negative.statement: The southeast square has limited staying quality, while the western garden remains spatially undecided and residual.

position.rationale: Southeast and western landscape areas are constrained by the building footprint and visible perimeter spaces.

negative.statement: The fitness area is awkwardly divided into two unconnected zones.

position.rationale: The fitness zones are interior and indistinguishable, so the marker uses a lower-level southeast approximation.

negative.statement: Innovative university operations are only rudimentarily represented in the floor plans.

position.rationale: Operational planning is not visible; the marker approximates an interior mid-level zone from the sampled envelope.

negative.statement: Noise from the foyer, meeting, and catering areas remains problematic, especially around the atrium.

position.target: foyer, meeting, and catering areas around the atrium
position.rationale: The central atrium is visible, while surrounding acoustic sources are inferred as adjacent internal zones.

negative.statement: The flexibility suggested by the floor plan is severely limited by restrictive fire-protection conditions.

position.rationale: Fire-protection constraints lack a visible element, so a distributed building-level approximation is used.

negative.statement: The facade evokes an office building and does not adequately represent the institution.

position.rationale: The repetitive cuboid facade is directly visible and comparable across all four elevations.

negative.statement: The large glass sheds lack delicacy, while the high glazing proportion is energetically unfavorable and difficult to clean.

position.rationale: Roof-level shed-like glazed elements are identified from the top silhouette and upper elevation bands.

negative.statement: Some teaching rooms receive no natural light, and other teaching rooms have unfavorable side lighting.

position.rationale: Teaching-room daylight conditions are not directly visible; placement is constrained to a south-side upper zone.

negative.statement: The building's usage density appears too high.

position.rationale: Density is a building-wide judgment, anchored to the visible overall mass and distributed envelope.

negative.statement: The delivery arrangement and bicycle parking are unsatisfactory.

position.rationale: Service and bicycle facilities are not distinguishable, so the southeast site edge provides a directional approximation.

negative.statement: The life-cycle costs exceed expectations and the energy concept is considered unsustainable.

position.rationale: Cost and energy performance judgments have no reliable spatial marker in the sampled geometry.
